sections.html: Xenopus muelleri grows to 7–8 cm in length (males stay about 20% smaller) and has a nice, spotted pattern. It is one of the smaller Xenopus species.

Most often Xenopus laevis is offered. This is the largest species of the genus and can reach the size of a man's hand. Frogs of that size are able to eat pretty big fish. However, there are also smaller species, such as Xenopus muelleri.
X. muelleri has an enormous range in tropical and subtropical Africa. The specimens described here, however, are European bred.

Clawed frogs (Xenopus) are popular aquarium inhabitants. They are totally aquatic animals and leave the water only for curiosity or when the water body dries out. Nevertheless the tank has to be absolutely safely covered, for a trip in the dry living room can cause the death of the animal.

Etymology: Xenopus is from ancient Greek and means "with a strange foot", referring to the three sharp claws on the hind foot. laevis is Latin and means "smooth, shining". muelleri is a dedication name.

It has been suggested that the frogs kept here might belong to a subspecies of X. laevis rather than to X. muelleri, because in X. muelleri even younger specimens should have much longer tentacles below the eye than these specimens.
